paths.blurb: Run an always-on, governed Kiro Crew for a team: schedules, Task Runner, workflows, apps, bots, Ops Mission Control, 24/7 hosting on AWS, any agent harness, knowledge and memory.

core.title: Spec → production feature
core.text: Turn a one-line prompt into EARS requirements, a design and a tracked task plan, then implement it wave by wave.

core.title: Guardrails on every save
core.text: Lint, test, secret-scan and doc-sync automatically with agent hooks.

core.title: A specialist agent per job
core.text: Reviewer, IaC author, release manager: scoped tools, permissions and context.

core.title: Infrastructure by conversation
core.text: Author and validate CDK / CloudFormation / Terraform with AWS IaC tooling over MCP.

core.title: Cost questions in plain English
core.text: Estimate before you build, explain the bill after you ship.

core.title: Agents in your pipeline
core.text: Headless Kiro reviews PRs, writes changelogs and fixes failing tests in CI.

core.title: Production agent hosting
core.text: Deploy any framework to serverless, session-isolated microVMs.

core.title: Any API becomes an MCP tool
core.text: Lambda, OpenAPI and Smithy targets behind one governed gateway.

core.title: Every persona has an agent
core.text: PM, architect, QA, SRE, FinOps, support and AI engineers each get a scoped Kiro agent with tenant-aware skills.

core.title: Tenant lifecycle on autopilot
core.text: Onboard, suspend and offboard tenants through one idempotent AWS CLI script driven by a skill and a Crew bot.

core.title: See every tenant and agent
core.text: Per-tenant metrics and agent traces in CloudWatch Omni, with DevOps Agent root cause.

core.title: AI features that respect tenants
core.text: Per-tenant inference profiles, filtered RAG, scoped memory and hard token budgets.

core.title: Morning briefing before standup
core.text: A weekday agent cron summarizes open PRs, red checks and assigned issues into a Slack DM, with --timezone set and no context piling up between runs.

core.title: Zero-token watchers
core.text: Script and command jobs check CI, disk or a status page without a model call, and only notify (or wake an agent) when something is wrong.

core.title: Watch it until it changes
core.text: A heartbeat line in HEARTBEAT.md watches a PR or deployment every 60 seconds and reports once the state changes, then clears itself.

core.title: Overnight, spec-driven changes
core.text: Task Runner turns a markdown spec into steps, runs each in a fresh session, tests, self-reviews and commits on its own branch for hours, pausing at force-approval steps.

core.title: Fan-out audits with a judge
core.text: An authored workflow runs one agent per file, a judge agent drops unreproducible findings, and the result lands as one versioned report.

core.title: PR babysitting without burning turns
core.text: monitor_watch watches a pull request through gh and wakes the agent only when CI or reviews change, until it is merge-ready.

core.title: Package a team's agent as an app
core.text: Ship an agent, a skill and a schedule as one app.json that teammates install from a folder or git URL.

core.title: Issue triage that remembers
core.text: Issue Radar summarizes and labels GitHub, GitLab or Azure DevOps issues and keeps investigation findings in a ledger so nothing is re-investigated.

core.title: Reviews weighted by blast radius
core.text: Code Review Sage reviews every changed file in an isolated session and publishes a prioritized Focus Report as a draft review only when you say so.

core.title: An AI first responder for alarms
core.text: Ops Mission Control claims CloudWatch alarms, investigates with your ambient AWS credentials, mirrors incidents to Slack and learns verified fixes.

core.title: A team assistant that never sleeps
core.text: Run Crew as a service, a signed container, or on your own EC2 instance launched with CloudFormation and reached over SSM with zero inbound ports.

core.title: Controls the agent can't weaken
core.text: Strict sandbox, denied commands, owner locks, a POLICY ∩ PROFILE ceiling distributed to every host, and a hash-chained audit log you can verify.

core.title: Runbooks the agent actually reads
core.text: Ingest runbooks and ADRs into the local knowledge library and get cited answers; corrections become lessons for every later session.

emerging.title: Always-on engineering bots
emerging.text: Intake, build-health, review and release-readiness bots with their own memory.

emerging.title: Issue → PR, unattended
emerging.text: Label an issue and let the autonomous agent deliver a reviewed pull request.

emerging.title: Deterministic tool policy
emerging.text: Cedar rules decide which tool calls an agent may make, with which arguments.

emerging.title: Agents that remember
emerging.text: Semantic, summary, preference and episodic memory across sessions.

emerging.title: Agent swarms & graphs
emerging.text: Orchestrate specialists with graph, swarm and agents-as-tools patterns.

emerging.title: Cross-framework agents
emerging.text: Agents talk to agents over A2A, regardless of who built them.

emerging.title: Continuous agent quality
emerging.text: Online evaluations on live traces catch regressions before users do.

emerging.title: Legacy to cloud-native
emerging.text: Spec-driven modernization of a monolith into serverless services.

emerging.title: Parity-verified migrations
emerging.text: Methodology as skills, a parity harness as referee, and a rulebook you fix instead of the code.

emerging.title: A coding agent that remembers
emerging.text: Kiro CLI with long-term memory in AgentCore Memory through your own MCP server.

emerging.title: Dozens of skills, small contexts
emerging.text: A skill-free coordinator routes to specialists that load only their own skills.

emerging.title: Plans that update themselves
emerging.text: Tasks from your project tool in the IDE; hooks sync status on commit.

emerging.title: An SDLC run by agents
emerging.text: Spec gate, isolation tests, AI review, cost diff and Security Agent on every PR, with humans at the gates.

emerging.title: Prompts shipped like code
emerging.text: Tier-aware routing, versioned prompts, canaries and eval-gated releases.

emerging.title: Start agent work from any system
emerging.text: An authenticated webhook (Feature Preview) lets a deploy pipeline or ticketing tool start a Crew session with a message.

emerging.title: Measured, keep-or-revert improvements
emerging.text: Auto-Improvement proves a metric first, then keeps only fixes whose measured win clears the noise band, drafted as PRs.

emerging.title: One workspace, any agent harness
emerging.text: Switch new sessions between the Kiro harness, Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode with a local model, while memory, schedules and apps stay put.

emerging.title: Unattended research campaigns
emerging.text: Research Lab expands a question into sub-questions, sends agents to each, and stops when answered or stalled, ending in a shareable report.

emerging.title: A whole team on one governed Crew
emerging.text: Slack as the front door, bots owning triage, CI and releases, apps in the dev loop, and weekly metrics on whether it helps.

emerging.title: Ticket in, canary out
emerging.text: A labelled issue flows from spec agent to parallel Kiro CLI builders, a verification mesh, the merge queue and a dark canary deploy with no human between label and production.

emerging.title: Self-healing main branch
emerging.text: A Crew bot bisects a red main, quarantines a flaky test with evidence and an expiry, and merges the fix through automated gates.

emerging.title: Autonomy that is earned and lost
emerging.text: A nightly job promotes or demotes each service's autonomy level from its error budget, revert and rollback rates, and the conductor reads it before dispatching work.

emerging.title: Rollback-first production verifier
emerging.text: After every deploy an agent compares SLOs and business metrics, rolls back on doubt, and files the root cause as the factory's next task.

crew.title: Pick up where you left off, anywhere
crew.text: Start a task in a Slack thread on your phone, continue it in the dashboard or desktop app, and finish from the CLI. It's the same Crew session, memory and lessons on every surface.

crew.title: Corrections that stick
crew.text: Say “no, always run the frontend checks first” once. Crew saves it as a lesson and applies it in later sessions, and `kirocrew learn list` shows what it learned.

crew.title: Framework upgrade marathon
crew.text: Hand the Task Runner a spec for a major-version upgrade. It works step by step on its own branch with tests after each step, commits what passes, and retries or replans what doesn't.

crew.title: Move your workspace in one command
crew.text: Snapshot every piece of Crew state (memory, schedules, apps, knowledge) and restore it on a new laptop or a remote EC2 crew with `kirocrew snapshot` and `kirocrew restore --dry-run`.

crew.title: Parallel research before a design decision
crew.text: Ask Crew to compare three libraries or AWS services in parallel. Each subagent researches one option in isolation, and the results come back as one comparison you can save as an artifact.

crew.title: Flaky-test hunter
crew.text: A Build health bot watches CI history, separates flaky failures from real ones with evidence, and proposes a quarantine with an expiry instead of silently retrying forever.

crew.title: Release readiness, owned by a bot
crew.text: A Release readiness bot runs the checklist (changelog, open blockers, CI status, migration notes) and reports in Slack, comment-only until it earns more trust.

crew.title: From a Slack thread to an approved spec
crew.text: Spec Builder turns a feature discussion into Requirements → Design → Tasks you review in-app, then hands the approved plan to an execution session.

crew.title: Docs that never drift
crew.text: A weekly workflow runs one agent per docs page to find outdated commands and broken links, a judge agent drops anything it can't reproduce, and one report lists what's left.

crew.title: On-call handover that writes itself
crew.text: Ops Mission Control's Handover tab lists what is waiting on a person, what stopped without a diagnosis and what keeps recurring, ready for the next responder.

crew.title: Cross-repo incident investigation
crew.text: When an incident spans services, Crew sends one subagent per repository to read recent changes and logs in parallel, then merges their findings into one timeline.

crew.title: Route work to the right specialist
crew.text: Define crews with their own agent, model, memory and trigger phrases. The orchestrator uses `select_crew` to send each request to the crew whose triggers match.

crew.title: Onboarding buddy in Slack
crew.text: New hires ask Crew questions in Slack. Answers come from the runbooks and ADRs in the knowledge library, with citations, so the same five questions stop reaching the team.

crew.title: Weekly engineering digest
crew.text: A Friday cron collects merged PRs, cycle time and open blockers from GitHub and posts a short digest to the team channel, with each claim linked.

crew.title: A team crew on your own AWS account
crew.text: Launch Crew on EC2 with `kirocrew cloud launch`: a CloudFormation stack, sign-in over SSM, no inbound ports and no AWS keys stored by Crew.

crew.title: Many crews, one hub
crew.text: Register remote crews under Settings → Remote Crew and manage them from one dashboard (multi-instance is a Preview feature).

crew.title: Ship your team's agent as an app
crew.text: Package an agent, a skill and a schedule as one `app.json` that every teammate installs from a git URL. Fix it once and everyone gets the update.

crew.title: One policy, every host
crew.text: Publish a `security_policy.json` ceiling at an internal URL and point every Crew host at it with `KIROCREW_POLICY_URL`. Profiles can narrow it but never widen it.

crew.title: Audit evidence on demand
crew.text: Every tool call and approval lands in an HMAC-chained security event log. `kirocrew security verify` proves the chain is intact and `security events` shows the decisions.

crew.title: Assistant on a local model
crew.text: Run new sessions on OpenCode with a local LM Studio or Ollama model for sensitive or offline work, while schedules, memory and the policy gate stay the same.

crew.title: Cost sentinel
crew.text: A scheduled bot reads AWS Billing data through MCP, explains day-over-day changes and pings the owner only when spend moves outside the expected range.

crew.title: Publish a prototype to your own AWS account
crew.text: Crew keeps versioned artifacts with live previews and can deploy one to your own AWS account. A publish policy limits destinations, Regions and accounts.
